title: What will Apple say during their next earnings call? Manufacturing
rules: If Manufacturing is said by any Apple representative (including the operator of the call) during the next Apple earnings call (including the Q+A), then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary:
How this is resolved
Video of the Apple earnings call.
If a consensus by Kalshi employees cannot be reached using video, transcripts of the Apple earnings call will be used according to the news publications listed in the contract. 

Payout criteria
The exact phrase/word, or a plural or possessive form of the phrase/word.

Doesn't count for payout
Grammatical/tense inflections.

Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the underlying company. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

blind.reasoning: Apple's next earnings call is November 2, 2026, before the market closes. Apple executives said 'manufacturing' several times in each recent call, mostly about the American Manufacturing Program, the Broadcom deal and the upcoming Houston Advanced Manufacturing Center. An update on that center and the U.S. investment program is very likely, even with a new CEO. The word also comes up often in Q&A about tariffs and supply chains.
blind.falsifier: John Ternus's first call on Nov 2 leaves out the U.S. investment/American Manufacturing Program section, and no Apple representative says 'manufacturing' in the Q&A (or the call is pushed past Nov 12).

final.reasoning: The market mid of 0.865 likely reflects the risk that the new CEO changes the script, so I've shaded my estimate down slightly. Repeated use of 'American Manufacturing Program', the pending update on the Houston center, and tariff/supply Q&A still put my probability above the 0.89 ask.
